summary.headline: Import pipeline gets a hard size cap, the flaky checkout test is quarantined rather than retried, and next week is a two-machine end-to-end run.
paragraphs: Most of the hour went to the import pipeline. Large files have been timing out somewhere past the eight-minute mark, and the temptation was to raise the timeout. The group went the other way: a hard cap on input size, a clear error naming the limit, and a documented path for the handful of genuinely large imports. The reasoning was that a timeout is a symptom you can keep raising forever, while a cap is a decision you make once and can explain to a customer.

The flaky checkout test came up again. It has been retried three times in CI for a month, which means it has effectively been off for a month while still costing everyone the wait. It gets quarantined with a linked ticket and an owner, on the principle that a test nobody trusts is worse than a test nobody has.

Next week's priority is a real two-machine end-to-end run rather than another round of local verification. Everything so far has passed on one developer's box, which is the configuration least likely to catch the bugs that matter.

decisions.text: Hard-cap import input at 512 MB. Reject above it with an error that names the limit and links the docs — no silent truncation, no raised timeout.
Quarantine the checkout test rather than retrying it. It gets a ticket and a named owner, and it does not gate merges until it is fixed.
Next milestone is a two-machine end-to-end run. A local pass no longer counts as evidence for this path.
